title: Sign-in history
purpose: See when your account signed in and out, and the attempts to sign in to it that failed or were refused, so you can spot anything you do not recognize.
summary: When your account signed in and out over the last 90 days, and the attempts to sign in to it that failed or were refused. Look for anything you do not recognize.

tasks.title: Check for sign-ins you do not recognize
steps: Open [[Sign-in history]] from the account menu.
Read the time, browser and address of each [[Signed in]] entry. [[This browser]] marks the sign-in of the session you are using now.
If one is not yours, sign it out on [[Where you are signed in]] and change your password. On a shared demonstration account others' sign-ins are expected.

tasks.title: Look into failed attempts
steps: Read the entries marked [[Sign-in failed]], [[Too many failed attempts]], [[Sign-in refused]] or [[Re-authentication failed]], and their [[Details]].
If you did not make them, change your password and tell your laboratory's security contact (portal users: the laboratory). A shared account's password cannot be changed.

tasks.title: Find out why you were signed out
steps: Find the [[Signed out]] entry at that time. [[Details]] says why, such as No activity, New password or Ended by an administrator.

good_to_know: Only you see your own history. A wrong password given with a name that matches no account, or several, is not listed for anyone.
No entry keeps what you typed: no password, no code, and not the username or email address entered.
The browser and the address are what the browser and the network reported, so they can be wrong.
Entries are never changed or deleted. The history starts at the release that added this page.
On a shared demonstration account, other visitors' entries are listed with the browser and address Not shown.

sections.title: Who can use this page
paragraphs: Every signed-in account, staff or client portal, opens it from the account menu (Sign-in history) or from the link at the foot of Where you are signed in. It lists only your own account's entries. Nobody else's history is shown to anyone in this release: there is no page where an administrator or a superuser reads it.

While your session must first set up a second sign-in factor, or choose a new password because yours was marked as compromised, the menu does not offer this page and opening it sends you back to that step.
The page is read-only. To end a session, use Where you are signed in.

items.label: When
items.description: The date and time of the entry, in the laboratory's time zone, by the database's clock. For a sign-out of a session that passed a session limit, the moment the limit passed, which can be earlier than the moment the sign-out was written (see Rules and records).

items.label: Event
items.description: What happened (see Events and details). Sign-in failed, Sign-in refused, Too many failed attempts and Re-authentication failed are shown as warnings. This browser marks the Signed in entry of the session you are reading the page from, not its other entries.

items.label: Details
items.description: For a sign-in, what it proved; for a failed attempt, what was not accepted; for a refusal or a sign-out, why. Not recorded when it is not known.

items.label: Browser
items.description: The browser and system, such as Firefox on Windows, worked out from how the browser described itself. Unknown browser when it gave nothing recognizable. For a sign-out, the browser the session reported when it signed in. Not shown on a shared demonstration account for entries of other sessions.

items.label: Address
items.description: The network address the request came from, as the deployment reports it; behind a proxy the deployment must be told which proxy to trust, or every entry shows the proxy's address. For a sign-out, the address the session reported when it signed in. Not recorded when no address was available. Not shown on a shared demonstration account for entries of other sessions.

items.label: Recent activity
items.description: The panel's title. The number beside it counts the entries shown.

items.label: Check the attempts that failed
items.description: A warning above the list when it shows any Sign-in failed, Sign-in refused, Too many failed attempts or Re-authentication failed entry. It says how many and what to do if you do not recognize them. Not shown on a shared demonstration account.

items.label: Nothing recorded yet
items.description: Shown when nothing was recorded for your account in the last 90 days, for example when you have not signed in since the release that added this page.

items.label: Signed in
items.description: A session started. Details: Password; Password and authenticator app; Password and recovery code; Emailed code; Emailed code and authenticator app; Emailed code and recovery code. Not recorded when the steps are not known, for example a session started by the earlier release still running while the deployment was upgraded.

items.label: Sign-in refused
items.description: The password, or an emailed code, was accepted, but the sign-in was not let through. Details: Password marked as compromised (the password alone was given while a superuser had marked it; the session ended as it started) or Account deactivated (the right password or an emailed code was given for a deactivated account, or the account was deactivated while the sign-in was under way; no usable session started). Recorded for the account the password or code was accepted for.

items.label: Sign-in failed
items.description: An attempt to sign in was not accepted. Details: Password not accepted; Authenticator or recovery code not accepted (the second step, which takes either kind of code); Emailed code not accepted.

items.label: Too many failed attempts
items.description: The failed sign-in limit refused the attempt before the password or code was checked, at sign-in or when a page asked for it again. Details: Refused before the password was checked, or Refused before the code was checked. Recorded at most once a minute for the same step and address: more refused attempts in that minute add no entry.

items.label: Re-authentication failed
items.description: While you were signed in, a page asked for your password or a code again and it was not accepted: the confirmation asked before a change such as setting up or removing an authenticator app, or the current password on Change password (also the admin console's own Change password). Details: Password not accepted, or Authenticator or recovery code not accepted.

items.label: Signed out
items.description: A session ended. Details says why: With Sign out (Sign out in the account menu, or Log out in the admin console); No activity; Longest session reached; Account deactivated; New password; Signed in again in the same browser; Signed out from another session (from Where you are signed in); Ended by an administrator; Password marked as compromised; A change found it past a limit (a change being saved found the session past a session limit, and the browser was signed out).

sections.title: What is and is not recorded
paragraphs: Every session's start and end is recorded, whichever way the session ended. A failed attempt, or one refused by the failed sign-in limit, is recorded only when the username or email address given names exactly one account, in any letter case; an attempt that names no account, or more than one, is not recorded in anyone's history and stays only in the deployment's sign-in log. A refused sign-in is recorded for the account whose password or emailed code was accepted. Failed codes and re-authentication failures belong to the account already identified at that step.
No entry holds a password, a code, or what was typed as the username or email address.

Not recorded: an attempt that the per-address request limit stopped before the form was read, an emailed code form sent without a code, a code entered after its emailed sign-in had expired, a request for an emailed code, and attempts handled by the earlier release's processes while a deployment replaces them (the sessions they start and end are recorded).
The browser and the address are what the request reported. They describe where the request seemed to come from and prove nothing on their own.

sections.title: Shared demonstration accounts
paragraphs: A shared demonstration account, one whose password the deployment publishes on the sign-in page, is used by other visitors too. Its history lists their entries as well, with the browser and the address shown only for the session you are using and Not shown for every other entry. An information notice says so, and the warning about failed attempts is not shown. Other visitors' sign-ins and failed attempts are expected there: the password cannot be changed and other visitors' sessions cannot be signed out from such an account.

sections.title: Rules and records
paragraphs: The list shows entries of the last 90 days by the database's clock, at most the 100 most recent, newest first.

Entries are never changed or deleted: the database refuses it. An account with sign-in history cannot be deleted; accounts are deactivated, not deleted. There is no retention period in the application: entries are kept.

A session's sign-in and sign-out are written by the database in the same step that starts or ends the session. A session that passed a session limit is recorded as signed out at the moment the limit passed, even when that is noticed later, for example when the account next signs in or a page of that session is next opened.
The history starts at the release that added it. A session already open then shows only its sign-out. The deployment's sign-in log is kept as before.

sections.title: If you do not recognize an entry
paragraphs: A sign-in you did not make: sign that session out on Where you are signed in, change your password from the account menu (that also ends your other sessions), and tell your laboratory's security contact, or the laboratory if you use the client portal. This does not apply to a shared demonstration account.

Failed attempts you did not make: someone may be trying your username or email address. Change your password if you think it could be known, and tell the same contact. An authenticator app on Two-factor authentication stops a known password signing in on its own. On a shared demonstration account the password and two-factor settings cannot be changed, and other visitors' failed attempts are expected.
Check the time zone and the times before concluding: a browser you forgot to sign out of ends with No activity or Longest session reached.
